sources: Distillery catalog + secondary-market series: Whisky Hunter (whiskyhunter.net), free public API
meta.note: Prices are typical retail bands, roughly: 1 value, 2 daily, 3 upgrade, 4 collector. Details vary by market.

regions.Islay: Peat, brine, and weather. A handful of wind-battered distilleries make the loudest flavours in whisky.
regions.Speyside: Half of Scotland's distilleries in one river valley. Sherry, orchard fruit, quiet confidence.
regions.Highland: The biggest region and the loosest definition: soft and honeyed to coastal and stern.
regions.Lowland: The gentle south: triple distillation, cut grass, citrus, and a tradition of being overlooked.
regions.Campbeltown: Once the whisky capital of the world with thirty distilleries; three stubborn survivors remain.
regions.Islands: Orkney to Arran: maritime malts from Scotland's scattered isles, each with salt in the glass.

countries.Scotland: The reference point. Single malt was built here, and the vocabulary of whisky is written in its regions.
countries.Ireland: Single pot still is the treasure: unmalted barley, spice, and cream. Also the oldest licensed distillery on earth.
countries.United States: Bourbon, rye, and a new wave of single malts. America's gift is sweetness from new charred oak.
countries.Japan: A century old and auction-mad. Precision, mizunara oak, and some of the most hunted bottles on the planet.
countries.Taiwan: Subtropical aging at speed. Kavalan proved a hot climate can make world-class malt.
countries.India: The world's largest whisky market, now making its own: tropical, rich, and increasingly serious.
countries.United Kingdom: England and Wales' returning wave; a century after the last English distillery closed, dozens are back.
countries.Sweden: The Nordic new wave: shorter seasons, long light, experimental casks.
countries.Australia: Wine-country energy and hot-climate aging; Melbourne's Starward led the charge.
countries.Canada: Blends built the country; a pure-rye revival is what's earning the respect now.

styles.Single Malt: Malt whisky from one distillery, in a pot still. The main event of the whisky world.
styles.Blended Malt: Malt whiskies from several distilleries, vatted together; no grain whisky involved.
styles.Blended Scotch: Malt plus grain, engineered like a symphony. The category that conquered the planet.
styles.Single Grain: One distillery, column stills, usually corn or wheat. Softness and structure.
styles.Irish Single Pot Still: Unmalted barley in the mash; the spicy, creamy soul of Irish whiskey.
styles.Irish Single Malt: Triple-distilled barleymalt, and none of the smoke (usually).
styles.Irish Blend: Grain and malt together; the friendly default of Dublin and beyond.
styles.Bourbon: At least 51% corn, new charred oak, and by law an American story.
styles.Tennessee Whiskey: Bourbon's cousin, filtered through charcoal before it ever sees a barrel.
styles.Rye: Spicy, herbal, and increasingly the bartender's chosen weapon.
styles.American Single Malt: The young domestic category: 100% malt barley, American oak, no rules borrowed.
styles.Japanese Single Malt: Precision-distilled, often finished in native mizunara oak. Tiny, hunted, magnificent.
styles.Japanese Blended Whisky: Suntory and Nikka's engineered calm; transparency in a bottle.
styles.Canadian Rye: Prairie rye with a softness all its own; the backbone of a century of cocktails.
styles.World Single Malt: Everything else, and it is increasingly serious: Taiwan, India, Australia, Wales, England, the Nordics.
